Bread.''] {{outside L|They imitate him not in vnleauened bread, and mingling vvater vvith vvine.}}Chri{{ls}}t made the holy Sacrament of vnleauened bread, and al the Latin Church imitateth him in the {{ls}}ame, as a thing much more agreable to the {{ls}}ignification both in it {{ls}}elf and in our liues, then the leauen. Yet our Aduer{{ls}}aries neither folovv Chri{{ls}}t, S. For Chri{{ls}}t and al the Apo{{ls}}tles and al Catholike Churches in the vvorld haue euer mixed their wine vvith water, for great my{{ls}}terie and {{ls}}ignification, {{ls}}pecially for that water gu{{ls}}hed together vvith bloud out of our Lordes {{ls}}ide. ''This our Lord did'' ({{ls}}aith S. Cyprian ''Ep. 63 ad Cecilium. nu. 4, 7''.) ''and none rightly offereth, that folovveth not him therein''. Thus Irenæus ''(li. 5. c. 1''.) Chri{{ls}}o{{ls}}toms: and yet our Prote{{ls}}tants pretending to reduce al to Chri{{ls}}t, vvil not doe as he did, and al the Apo{{ls}}tles and Churches that euer vvere.

''24. My body.''] {{outside L|The Prote{{ls}}tants haue taken avvay the B. Sacrament altogether.}}Vvhen the vvordes of Con{{ls}}ecration be by the {{ls}}aid impietie of the Prote{{ls}}tants, thus remoued from the elements: no maruel if Chri{{ls}}tes holy body and bloud be not there, or that it is novv no more a Sacrament, but common bread and vvine. So they that vniu{{ls}}tly charge the Cath. Church vvith defrauding the people of one peece of the Sacrament, haue in very deede left no part nor {{ls}}pice of Sacrament, neither folovving Chri{{ls}}t, as they pretend, nor S. Paul, nor any Euangeli{{ls}}t, but their ovvne dete{{ls}}table Secte, hauing boldly defaced the vvhole in{{ls}}titution, not in any accidental indifferent circun{{ls}}tances, but in the very {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance and al. The right name is gone, the due elements both gone, no ble{{ls}}{{ls}}ing or con{{ls}}ecration, or other action ouer them, the formes be gone: and con{{ls}}equently the body and bloud, the Sacrament and the Sacrifice.

''24. This doe.''] {{outside L|The povver to con{{ls}}ecrate giuen to Prie{{ls}}ts onely.}}By the{{ls}}e vvordes, authoritie and povver is giuen to the Apo{{ls}}tles, and by the like, in the Sacrament of Orders, to al lavvful Prie{{ls}}ts onely. ''24. Take and eate.''] This pertaineth to the receiuing of tho{{ls}}e things vvhich by con{{ls}}ecration are pre{{ls}}ent and {{ls}}acrificed before: as vvhen the people or Prie{{ls}}ts in the old Lavv did eate the ho{{ls}}tes offered or part thereof, they vvere made partakers of the {{ls}}acrifice done to God before. {{outside L|The Sacrament con{{ls}}i{{ls}}teth not in the receiuing.}}And this is not the {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance, or being, or making of the Sacrament or Sacrifice of Chri{{ls}}tes body and bloud: but it is the v{{ls}}e and application to the receiuer, of the things vvhich vvere made and offered to God before. There is a difference betvvixt the making of a medecine or the {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance and ingredience of it, and the taking of it. Novv the receiuing being but a con{{ls}}equence or one of the endes vvhy the Sacrament vvas made, & the meane to apply it vnto vs: {{outside L|Vvhy the Prote{{ls}}tants call it the Communion.}}the Aduer{{ls}}aries vnlearnedly make it al and {{ls}}ome, ad therfore improperly name the vvhole Sacrament and mini{{ls}}tration therof, by calling it the Communion. Vvhich name they giue al{{ls}}o rather then any other, to make the ignorant beleeue that many mu{{ls}}t communicate together: as though it vvere {{ls}}o called for that it is common to many. By which collu{{ls}}ion they take avvay the receiuing of the Prie{{ls}}t alone, of the {{ls}}icke alone, of re{{ls}}eruing the con{{ls}}ecrated Ho{{ls}}t and the vvhole Sacrament. {{outside L|Communion, vvhich is a part of the {{sc|Masse}}, vvhat it {{ls}}ignifieth.}}Again{{ls}}t vvhich deceite, knovv that this part of the {{sc|Masse}} is not called Communion, for that many {{ls}}hould concurre together alwaies in the external Sacrament: but for that vve do<noinclude>{{continues|communicate}}
